title: Apply Operations in Order
description: You are given a starting integer x and a list of operations. Each operation is a string: "add n", "sub n" or "mul n", where n is an integer. Apply the operations to x in order and return the final value. Consider writing a small helper function that applies one operation.
constraints: 0 <= len(ops) <= 100, intermediate values fit in a normal integer
hints: str.split() separates the operation name from its number.
Write a helper function that takes the current value and one operation string and returns the new value.

title: Validate Binary Search Tree
description: A binary tree is given as a level-order list: the root first, then each level from left to right, with None for a missing node. Children of a missing node are not listed. Return True if it is a valid binary search tree: for every node, all values in its left subtree are strictly smaller and all values in its right subtree are strictly larger. Duplicates make a tree invalid. An empty tree is valid.

examples.explanation: Node 4 is in the right subtree of 5 but is smaller than 5.

hints: First turn the level-order list into nodes that have left and right children.
Comparing a node only with its direct children is not enough. Pass down a lower and an upper bound that every value in the subtree must respect.

title: Level Order Sums
description: A binary tree is given as a level-order list: the root first, then each level from left to right, with None for a missing node. Children of a missing node are not listed. Return a list containing the sum of the node values on each level, from the top level down. An empty tree returns an empty list.

examples.explanation: Level 1 is 3, level 2 is 9 + 20 = 29, level 3 is 15 + 7 = 22.

hints: Handle one level at a time. Keep the list of real nodes on the current level.
Each real node on a level takes the next two entries of the list as its children. Skip the None entries when building the next level.

title: Reverse Linked List Segment
description: A singly linked list is given as a Python list of node values from head to tail. Given positions left and right (1-indexed, left <= right), reverse the nodes from position left to position right and return the resulting list of values.
hints: Positions are 1-indexed, but list indices start at 0.
In a real linked list you would walk to the node before position left, then reverse the next right - left + 1 nodes by re-pointing links.
reference_solution:
def solve(nums, left, right):
    return nums[:left - 1] + nums[left - 1:right][::-1] + nums[right:]

title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
description: Given a string s, return the length of the longest substring that contains no repeated character. An empty string returns 0.

examples.explanation: The longest such substring is "abc", with length 3.

hints: Keep a window [left, right] that never contains a repeat.
Remember the last index at which each character was seen. When you meet a repeat inside the window, move left just past its previous position.

title: Three Sum
description: Given a list of integers, return all unique triplets [a, b, c] whose values add up to 0. Each triplet must be sorted in ascending order, no triplet may appear twice, and the list of triplets must be sorted in ascending order (comparing triplets like lists). Return an empty list if there are none.

examples.explanation: These are the only two distinct triplets that sum to 0.

hints: Sort the list first.
Fix one number, then use two pointers (one from each end) on the rest to find pairs that cancel it.
Skip repeated values for the fixed number and for the pointers so no triplet is reported twice.

title: Minimum Eating Speed
description: There are several piles of bananas, piles[i] bananas in pile i. You have h hours. Each hour you pick one pile and eat up to k bananas from it. If the pile has fewer than k bananas you finish it and eat nothing more that hour. Return the smallest integer k that lets you eat every banana within h hours. It is guaranteed that h >= len(piles).

examples.explanation: At speed 4 the piles take 1 + 2 + 2 + 3 = 8 hours. At speed 3 they would take 10.

hints: For a given speed k, the hours needed are the sum of ceil(pile / k) over all piles.
A higher speed never takes more hours, so you can binary search over k between 1 and the largest pile.

title: Course Schedule Order
description: There are n courses numbered 0 to n - 1. Each prerequisite is a pair [a, b], meaning course b must be taken before course a. Return an order in which all courses can be taken. Because several valid orders may exist, use this rule: at every step, take the available course (all its prerequisites already taken) with the smallest number. If it is impossible to take all courses because of a cycle, return an empty list. No pair appears twice.

examples.explanation: Only 0 is available first. Then 1 and 2 are available and 1 is smaller. Then 2, then 3.

hints: Count how many prerequisites each course still needs (its in-degree).
Keep the courses with zero remaining prerequisites in a min-heap. Pop the smallest, add it to the order, and reduce the count of the courses that depend on it.
If you finish with fewer than n courses in the order, there is a cycle.
reference_solution:
def solve(n, prerequisites):
    import heapq
    adj = [[] for _ in range(n)]
    indeg = [0] * n
    for a, b in prerequisites:
        adj[b].append(a)
        indeg[a] += 1
    heap = [i for i in range(n) if indeg[i] == 0]
    heapq.heapify(heap)
    out = []
    while heap:
        u = heapq.heappop(heap)
        out.append(u)
        for v in adj[u]:
            indeg[v] -= 1
            if indeg[v] == 0:
                heapq.heappush(heap, v)
    return out if len(out) == n else []

title: Merge K Sorted Lists
description: Given a list of k lists, each sorted in ascending order (some may be empty), return a single sorted list containing every value from all of them. Aim for O(N log k), where N is the total number of values.

examples.explanation: All values merged in sorted order.

hints: Merging the lists one after another is slow when k is large.
Keep a min-heap holding the current front value of each list. Pop the smallest, then push the next value from the same list.

title: Longest Common Subsequence
description: A subsequence keeps the original order of characters but may skip some (for example "ace" is a subsequence of "abcde"). Given two strings a and b, return the length of their longest common subsequence.
hints: Let cell (i, j) be the answer for the first i letters of a and the first j letters of b.
If a[i-1] equals b[j-1], the cell is the diagonal cell plus 1. Otherwise it is the larger of the cell above and the cell to the left.

title: Subsets With Duplicates
description: Given a list of integers that may contain duplicates, return all possible unique subsets (the power set without repeated subsets). Each subset must be sorted in ascending order, and the list of subsets must be sorted in ascending order (comparing subsets like lists, so [] comes first and [1] comes before [1, 2]).

examples.explanation: Two 2s are interchangeable, so [1, 2] is listed once.

hints: Sort the list first so equal values sit next to each other.
Build subsets by choosing which element to add next, moving forward only.
At one recursion level, skip a value if it equals the previous value at that same level, which avoids repeated subsets.
